key_insight: Update-matched unlearning (UMU) prevents a model from relearning deleted knowledge without sacrificing its ability to learn new tasks.
engineering_relevance: For deployed LLMs that keep evolving after release, UMU offers a safer update strategy that preserves plasticity while maintaining unlearning protections.
method: Apply the same simulated relearning update to both the defended model and an undefended reference initialized from the same unlearned model.
Use an update-matched reference rather than a pre-update reference to judge whether the model should stay close after an update.
Select models using performance on new tasks to balance suppression and adaptability.
evidence_signal: On TOFU and FaithUn with Llama and Qwen models, UMU improved relearning resistance and plasticity across three base unlearning methods, reducing harmful and benign relearning by 30.4 and 9.9 points on average while increasing new-task accuracy by 3.5 points.
watch_item: Results depend on the choice of update simulation and reference timing, so using a pre-update reference may falsely penalize beneficial learning and reduce plasticity.
paper_title: Not All Change Is Damage: Update-Matched Unlearning for Large Language Models
